start_here: Say to your AI: "Hear my recording /Recordings/sample-talk.wav on this computer with the whisper model I granted and give me its words with times." It runs tool:hear-a-recording and hands back the text and timed segments.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of its own: it reads one recording through the files door and answers the words it heard.
instructions: 1. Install whisper-cli and ffmpeg on your computer and keep one ggml Whisper model file in the models folder you granted.
2. Say "Hear my recording /Recordings/sample-talk.wav", and give the model file as model_path.
3. The AI runs tool:hear-a-recording with {file, model_path}; the door reads the recording into the run folder, hears it there and removes the copy.
4. Read what comes back: text, segments (start, end, text), language, heard_whole and produced_by. Without file or model_path it refuses before reading anything.

worked_examples.title: A five-second sample talk is heard into two timed segments
worked_examples.ask: Hear my recording /Recordings/sample-talk.wav and give me its words with times.
worked_examples.given: From the sample-run in tools/audio-transcription/tool-rows.json (verify) and tools/audio-transcription/test/hear-a-recording.test.mjs: the file holds made-up sound bytes and the stand-in whisper-cli writes two segments (0 to 2500 ms and 2500 to 5000 ms). The answer was worked out from read-data/hear-here.mjs (hearARecording, hearFile), not run here.
